item.title: EC secretary: First phase of local polls to cover 1,050 union parishads
item.description:
The Election Commission (EC) plans to hold the first phase of the upcoming local government elections in 1,050 union parishads (UPs), Senior Secretary of the EC Secretariat Akhtar Ahmed said.
He disclosed the matter while speaking to reporters at the Election Commission headquarters in Agargaon, Dhaka, on Sunday.
Akhtar Ahmed said the commission is prioritising union parishads whose terms have expired and is preparing to hold elections in slightly more than 1,050 unions.
He also said the commission is considering collecting information for National Identity (NID) registration from children as young as six.
"We are discussing creating a database using the information provided when children enter primary school," he said.
The EC secretary said electronic voting machines (EVMs) would not be used in the upcoming elections.
The commission has begun a final stocktaking of the machines ahead of their disposal, he said, adding that the disposal method would be determined after receiving recommendations on the matter.

item.title: Riyadh financial district targeted, Aramco skyscraper damaged
item.description:
An Aramco building in Riyadh was targeted in an “attempted attack,” the Saudi energy ministry said on Sunday, with eyewitnesses telling AFP the skyscraper sustained damage, after the Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen’s Houthis said it had intercepted missiles launched by the group.
Aramco facilities and infrastructure have been repeatedly struck by the Houthis in recent months, with tankers, refineries, storage areas and the company headquarters all targeted by the group.
“Aramco tower in Kafd has been targeted, that’s the sure thing,” an eyewitness told AFP, referring to the King Abdullah Financial District. Two other witnesses confirmed seeing damage to the building.
A 2022 truce that had paused fighting in Yemen’s long-running conflict fell apart in July and Saudi Arabia has since traded blows with the Houthis, who have struck Saudi airports, energy infrastructure and military sites.
The Iran-backed Houthis seized the Yemeni capital Sanaa in 2014, with the Saudi-led coalition entering the conflict a year later in support of the government.
One eyewitness in the area of the Aramco skyscraper told AFP they saw a projectile strike the building but they were unsure what type of projectile it was.
The King Abdullah Financial District is one of the most visible manifestations of the kingdom’s ongoing economic and social reforms drive, with towering glass skyscrapers, high-end retail outlets and green spaces dotting the area.
Kafd is home to some of the kingdom’s biggest home-grown companies and blue-chip international firms like Goldman Sachs.
The headquarters of the kingdom’s influential sovereign wealth fund -- the Public Investment Fund -- and the Saudi stock exchange are also located in the heart of the district.
Targeting the area, which is also home to residential housing and a large metro station with heavy commuter traffic during the morning rush hour, would mark a major escalation in the kingdom’s fight with the Houthis.
Multiple floors of the Aramco tower appeared to have sustained damage, said another witness, with glass shattered and damage to part of the tower’s facade visible.
The energy ministry said in a statement that “an administrative building belonging to Saudi Aramco in Riyadh was subjected to an attempted attack today”.
“The incident resulted in falling shrapnel that caused minor damage to the building, with no injuries or fatalities reported, thankfully.”
AFP was unable to confirm the extent of the damage.
The kingdom’s interior ministry has repeatedly warned residents against filming and publishing images of drones, missiles, air defense interceptors and the impacts of barrages.
The attack comes hours after the kingdom’s education ministry announced, late on Saturday, the return of in-person schooling after weeks of remote-learning in Riyadh following an earlier wave of strikes.
Coalition spokesperson Turki al-Malki, in a Sunday morning social media post, said that “air defenses intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched by the Houthi terrorist militia towards Riyadh”, as loud explosions were heard in the Saudi capital.
The kingdom has been pressing allies for help as it comes under daily fire from the Houthis that recently seized swathes of the Red Sea coastline from the Riyadh-backed government.
Thousands of Syrian troops are set to deploy to Saudi Arabia and Yemen, with some already on the ground, multiple Yemeni officials told AFP.
The United Nations says more than 1,600 people have been killed and more than 300,000 displaced since fighting resumed in impoverished Yemen.
The fragile 2022 truce fell apart after the Houthis allowed an Iranian plane to land in Yemen’s capital Sanaa in defiance of Saudi control over Yemeni airspace, setting off a spate of attacks.
Later, the Houthis declared a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia and began hitting its ships, territory and oil facilities, before seizing Yemen’s entire Red Sea coast in a lightning campaign.

item.title: Over 50 blasts, 8 buses torched: Who is behind Dhaka's terror?
item.description:
Panic gripped the Dhaka University campus on Sunday evening as a series of crude bomb explosions, which also struck several other locations across the capital, deepened public fear.
The evening rush had not yet subsided on campus when two loud explosions rang out in quick succession in the TSC area. Similar blasts followed beside the administrative building, in front of the VC Chattar and at the Mukti-Ganatantra Toron. Students detained several people as they fled the scene.
Elsewhere in the capital that evening, crude bombs also exploded at several other locations, including in front of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) office in Malibagh.
The night before, after 1am, two people on a motorcycle fled after setting off three to four crude bombs in succession at the Chowrasta intersection in Jatrabari. A few hours earlier, another bomb exploded in front of the upazila parishad gate at Genda Bus Stand on the Dhaka-Aricha Highway in Savar. Eyewitnesses could not identify who carried it out.
Explosions are now occurring one after another across the capital and surrounding areas, in front of police stations, at police facilities, near important government buildings and on university campuses. Some attackers arrive on motorcycles, set off explosions and flee. In other cases, their movements are captured on CCTV. After each incident, police say they are investigating, conducting operations and trying to identify those responsible.
Questions remain, however, about who is behind the blasts and how directly the detained individuals are linked to them. Are police identifying and arresting the people who throw the bombs, or are arrests mainly of suspects and people accused of political affiliations, to fill arrest figures? And who is making and supplying the bombs, and directing the attacks?
A review of recent incidents shows suspects were detained during the explosion or while fleeing in several cases. In statements after most of the widely discussed incidents, however, police spoke of attackers escaping, efforts to identify them and ongoing investigations. Police claim a group is carrying out the incidents to deliberately spread panic among the public.
At least 8 buses have been set on fire and more than 50 crude bomb explosions reported at different locations in the capital over the past few days. At least 8 bombs exploded between Friday (November 6) evening and late at night, in Adabor, Shahbagh, Khilgaon, the Airport area and Kalshi in Mirpur.
The previous day, Thursday (November 5) night, two explosions occurred in front of Pan Pacific Sonargaon Hotel and in front of Gate 3 of Rajarbagh Police Lines. No information was available about anyone being detained in connection with those incidents. On November 2, a crude bomb also exploded near Dhanmondi Government Boys’ High School in Sobhanbagh.
On Saturday (November 7) night, a crude bomb was thrown at the Setu Bhaban in Banani, breaking the glass of its guard room. Police recovered another unexploded bomb from the scene. Banani police station OC Md Salauddin said efforts were underway to identify the attackers. An explosion was also reported in the Sher-e-Bangla Agricultural University area later that night.
Among recent incidents, the October 30 blast in Kalabagan stands out. Police arrested four people during the explosion and as they tried to flee. Police said those arrested included activists of the banned Awami League and Jubo League. Police initially recovered three crude bombs and later recovered another 10 unexploded bombs based on information provided by the arrested individuals.
According to police, a bomb was also thrown at the Dhanmondi police station OC, who had gone to the scene after hearing the explosion. He detained two people, and the other two were arrested by Kalabagan police station. In this case, there is information linking the arrested individuals to the scene and to the recovery of explosives.
Separately, police on October 30 arrested two people, after analysing CCTV footage, in connection with a crude bomb explosion in front of the old Ramna police station on October 23. Four crude bombs were recovered based on information they provided.
Earlier police investigations have also raised allegations of bombs being thrown in exchange for money. Rezaul Islam was arrested in connection with an explosion in front of the office of the Investigation Agency of the International Crimes Tribunal on September 30. The then Dhanmondi police station OC, Muhammad Imdadul Islam, claimed that a political party whose activities were banned had offered him Tk 50,000 to throw a crude bomb. Police provided this information based on his initial interrogation.
This indicates that the person throwing a bomb, the person financing the attack and the person giving instructions may not be the same individual. However, it has not been established whether that earlier incident has any connection with the November explosions.
Responding to journalists’ questions at the DMP Media Centre on Minto Road on Sunday (November 8), Deputy Police Commissioner (Media and Public Relations) Md Akhtar Hossain said police were closely monitoring and investigating every incident of bomb explosions and vehicle arson. Several people have already been arrested, among them members of various banned organisations and their affiliated bodies.
He said that, after reviewing the incidents as a whole, police believed a particular group was deliberately carrying out sabotage and spreading panic among the public. Operations and police deployment had been intensified based on intelligence information, and mobile patrols, picket duty and surveillance were continuing.
Asked about the source of the materials used to make the bombs, Akhtar Hossain said the Detective Branch had previously arrested several people along with explosive materials and ingredients used to make crude bombs. Police were monitoring whether flammable materials were being bought and sold anywhere for sabotage, and efforts were underway to identify those involved by analysing CCTV footage.
Information from the incidents in Adabor, Shahbagh, the Airport area, Kalshi and Jatrabari indicates that individuals arrived on motorcycles, carried out the explosions and fled. Video footage is available in some cases. However, the information made public does not indicate confirmed progress in identifying and arresting the bombers in all the incidents.
It is therefore necessary to investigate whether a common criminal group is behind similar attacks in multiple areas. Investigators also need to establish where the bombs are being made, who is transporting them, where the instructions are coming from and who is arranging the attackers’ escape.
Dr Tawhidul Haque, a Dhaka University teacher and crime analyst, told Dhaka Tribune that arrests were important for maintaining law and order, but it was equally necessary to ensure that innocent people were not harassed on the basis of suspicion. He said no arrested individual should be presented as a bomb thrower without proper evidence in the investigation.

item.title: Fourth session of Parliament to continue till November 18
item.description:
The fourth session of the current parliament, which is set to begin on Monday afternoon after 60 days of the prorogation of the previous session, will continue till November 18 next.
During the fourth session, the parliament will sit at 4:20pm every day except Fridays and Saturdays.
The decision was taken at a meeting of the Parliamentary Business Advisory Committee held at the Cabinet Room of the National Parliament on Sunday, a day ahead of the commencement of the session.
Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad, Bir Bikram, chaired the meeting, while Prime Minister and Leader of the House Tarique Rahman attended it.
The meeting discussed the allocation of time for conducting parliamentary business and the duration of the fourth session of the 13th Parliament.
It was also decided that the Speaker would be authorized to make any changes to the sitting schedule and working days of the session, if necessary.
Committee members --Leader of the Opposition Md Shafiqur Rahman, Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed, Deputy Speaker Barrister Kayser Kamal, Chief Whip Md. Nurul Islam, Law Minister Md Asaduzzaman, BNP standing committee member Goyasawar Chandra Roy, Jamaat leader ATM Azharul Islam and Opposition Chief Whip Md Nahid Islam also attended the meeting.
According to the meeting, one government bill has so far been received for placement in the House during the fourth session.
Besides, three ordinances issued between the third and fourth sessions will be placed before Parliament at its first sitting.
The ordinances are the Public Procurement (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026, the Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026, and the Special Solar Power Installation Ordinance, 2026.
A total of 3,751 questions have been received for the session, including 174 for the Prime Minister and 3,577 for other ministers.
Besides, 92 notices have been received under Rule 71 of the Rules of Procedure for drawing the attention of ministers to matters of public importance, while 281 notices have been submitted under Rule 131 of the Rules of Procedure seeking decisions on various proposals.
During the meeting, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman proposed declaring the National Parliament premises a smoke-free area. The proposal was unanimously welcomed by the committee members.
The prime minister also enquired about the progress of the sound system at the parliament building.
In response, Parliament Secretary Barrister Md Golam Sorwar Bhuiyan informed him that the sound system would be inaugurated at 3:30pm on Monday under the supervision of the Public Works Department.
The prime minister also enquired about the progress of installing solar panels at the National Parliament.
In response, Deputy Speaker Barrister Kayser Kamal, who is the convener of the relevant subcommittee, informed the meeting that the proposed solar power system would be capable of generating 7 megawatts of electricity.
He said the electricity generated would be sufficient to meet the Parliament's demand during session periods, when consumption stands at around 6 megawatts, while demand remains lower at other times.
The surplus electricity would be supplied to the national grid.
The prime minister directed the authorities concerned to ensure that the solar power generation system includes electricity storage facilities.
On October 14 last, President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir summoned the session in exercise of the powers conferred upon him under Article 72(1) of the Constitution of Bangladesh.
According to the Article 72 (1) of the Constitution, a period exceeding 60 days shall not intervene between the end of one session and the first sitting of Parliament in the next session.
Earlier, the third session was prorogued on September 10 last after only nine sittings, the second session, also known as the budget session, was prorogued on July 15 after 27 working days.
During the budget session, parliament passed the Tk 938,000-crore national budget for the 2026-27 fiscal year, the first budget under the current BNP government.
The first session of the parliament commenced on March 12, following the general election held on February 12, 2026.
During its first session, parliament passed 94 bills, including 91 bills against ordinances promulgated during the interim government’s tenure, and formed several parliamentary committees.

item.title: ‘I am deeply sorry’: Nvidia stock falls as Jensen Huang’s affair and an alleged spying scandal rocks the AI industry
item.description:
Shares in Nvidia Corporation (Nasdaq: NVDA) are sinking today, less than 12 hours after CEO Jensen Huang publicly confirmed that he’d had an extramarital affair, and after the chipmaker confirmed that it was investigating Huang’s relationship amid reports that the woman he’d had an affair with was allegedly spying on behalf of Beijing.

The story has rocked the AI industry at a time when related tech stocks are already facing their most significant headwinds since the artificial intelligence boom first took off. Here’s everything you need to know to get caught up.

Huang and Nvidia confirm affair and investigation

Last night, Nvidia published a statement from its board of directors confirming that the company has launched an independent investigation into its CEO, Jensen Huang.

The statement came following earlier reports by the New York Times and the Financial Times alleging that Huang had been having an extramarital affair with Alice Huang, a senior leader at a Singapore-based cloud company called Megaspeed.

U.S. intelligence services believe the woman was spying on behalf of China, the reports said.

Nvidia makes the world’s most advanced chips and graphics cards, which are now the backbone of the AI revolution.

For years, the company’s most state-of-the-art technology has faced export restrictions to China over national security fears. The United States and China are locked in an AI arms race, and U.S. lawmakers and national security experts worry that the sale of Nvidia’s hardware to China would give the country an edge economically and militarily.

While the extramarital affair stands to damage Huang’s personal reputation, AI industry insiders, Wall Street, and security experts are most concerned about the fact that Huang’s companion may have also been working as an intelligence operative.

There are fears that any industry information or Nvidia secrets that Jensen Huang may have discussed with Alice Huang could have been passed along to foreign intelligence services.

After Huang confirmed the affair—and Nvidia confirmed the investigation—Nvidia’s stock sank in premarket trading on Monday. This is more bad news for investors who have already seen AI-related stocks get hammered in the past week.

Fast Company reached out to Megaspeed for comment. It was not immediately clear if Alice Huang, who could not be reached for comment, still worked there.

What has Jensen Huang said?

When reports of the affair first broke, Jensen Huang suggested that he’d had only had normal business engagements with Alice Huang. The two had been photographed together at multiple business and social events.

But last night, Huang sent an email to Nvidia employees confirming the affair. Nvidia later published the message on its website. 

“I owe my family and all of you an apology,” the message began. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”

Addressing Nvidia employees directly, Huang said, “you deserve better from me. Leading NVIDIA is the privilege of my life. My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility. I am fully committed to NVIDIA and will work to earn back your confidence.”

Huang also addressed the national security concerns about his affair, saying the company had launched an independent investigation.

“I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American,” Huang added.

Huang, who cofounded Nvidia in 1993, has been seen as one of the single most influential tech leaders behind the AI revolution.

What has Nvidia said?

Nvidia confirmed that its board of directors has initiated an independent investigation into the reports that Huang may have “been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.” 

The investigation will be led by “independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel,” according to the company, with the board noting that it “prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders.”

The company also stated that its board of directors has no reason to believe the company’s secrets or national security were compromised. 

Nvidia says that it still has “confidence in Jensen and his leadership team.”

What have China and the U.S. said?

Officials in China were quick to dispute the reports that it targeted Nvidia’s CEO in any way. Reuters quoted Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun as saying, “The so-called Chinese spy narrative is purely a groundless accusation, slander, and a smear.”

As for U.S. officials, when reporters asked Secretary of State Marco Rubio about the matter, he replied: “Yeah, I can’t comment on any of that. I just can’t comment because of the nature of it.  And I also can’t comment on an internal corporate matter that’s going on with Nvidia.”

President Trump told reporters, “I have not spoken to [Jensen Huang] about it. I just know he’s a fine person, but you never know what is going on.” He added: ”I hope everything’s fine.”

The president also said, “I think he’s an honorable guy,” noting that the Nvidia CEO had “done an amazing job for our country.”

How has NVDA stock reacted?

Not well. As of this writing, in premarket trading, Nvidia shares are down more than 5% to just above $177. If today’s premarket drop holds, Nvidia will have lost more than 26% of its value in the past month alone.

Like many AI-related stocks last week, Nvidia shares sank in the days after the 2026 U.S. midterm election results, amid fears that the incoming Democratic-led Congress would take a more cautious approach to AI data center buildouts than the current administration. Voters have overwhelmingly shown their distaste for the massive server farms.

Huang’s scandal is sure to do no favors to the larger AI industry, which is already facing worries about a stock market bubble and growing unpopularity with the broader public.

What happens next?

Nvidia likely won’t be the only entity investigating the allegations.

Dan Ives, senior managing director at Yorkville Ives & Co, told CNBC, “This is a black eye moment for Jensen and will spark multiple congressional inquiries at a minimum and will create an overhang on the stock for a myriad of reasons.”

Ives believes there is a risk Jensen could be removed from his CEO position at Nvidia. 

“[T]his will add risk to the stock as he is so important to the Nvidia story and strategy globally.”

item.title: Pakistan beat Nepal to set up U-19 Asia Cup semi-final against Bangladesh
item.description:
Defending champions Pakistan maintained their unbeaten run in the ACC Men’s U-19 Asia Cup 2026 with a convincing 101-run victory over Nepal at the Al Amerat Cricket Ground in Muscat on Tuesday.

With three wins from as many matches, Pakistan finished top of Group A to qualify for the semi-finals, where they will take on Bangladesh in the first semi-final on Thursday.

Batting first, Pakistan posted 275-7 in their allotted 50 overs, with half-centuries from Ahmed Hussain and captain Farhan Yousaf laying the foundation for the total.

Ahmed top-scored with a brisk 89 off 73 balls, hitting seven fours and two sixes, while Farhan contributed 74 off 95 balls, including six fours and three sixes.

The pair steadied the innings after Pakistan had slipped to 64-3, adding 135 runs for the fourth wicket. Hasnain Abbas Dar provided late impetus with a quick-fire 25 off 23 balls.

For Nepal, Bipin Sharma took three wickets for 58 runs.

In reply, Nepal were bowled out for 174 in 43.4 overs. Ahmed completed an impressive all-round performance, claiming four wickets for 35 runs in his 10 overs. Mohammad Huzaifa and Mohammad Sayyam took two wickets each.

Rohit Chand was Nepal’s top scorer with 37.

item.title: Bangladesh prosecutor says ex-PM Sheikh Hasina will be executed if she returns
item.description:
The Bangladeshi prosecutor who secured the death sentence against ousted leader Sheikh Hasina said on Tuesday she will be executed if she returns home.

Hasina, whose 15-year rule was ended by a mass uprising she tried to crush, has vowed to return in December to Bangladesh, where she was convicted of crimes against humanity over the 2024 crackdown on protesters.

“Sheikh Hasina has no option but to face the execution of the verdict,” Md Aminul Islam told reporters, responding to reports she planned to return from self-imposed exile in neighbouring India.

He added that the 79-year-old fugitive had missed the deadline to appeal against her conviction, leaving her with no further legal recourse.

“The statutory appeal period has expired and no appeal can now be filed,” he said.

The daughter of a revolutionary who led Bangladesh to independence in 1971, Hasina presided over breakneck economic growth, helping transform the South Asian nation of 170 million people from a largely agricultural economy into a global manufacturing hub.

Critics have accused Hasina of jailing political rivals, enacting harsh anti-press laws and overseeing widespread human rights abuses, including the killing of opposition activists.

Her 2024 crackdown left up to 1,400 people dead, according to the United Nations.

She fled to neighbouring India by helicopter in August 2024 as angry crowds stormed her palace.

She has remained there ever since, hidden from public view. Only occasionally has she addressed news conferences by telephone, her voice sounding frail.

Hasina has repeatedly said she intends to return to Bangladesh in December, telling AFP she is “fully aware” she faces being hanged if she returns.

She said “fear cannot decide” her “duty to the people”.

Extradition process

Hasina defied orders from the court to return to Bangladesh to attend her trial last year on whether she bore command responsibility for the bloody crackdown on the student-led uprising.

Witnesses included a man whose face was ripped apart by a gunshot.

Hasina, who was assigned a state-appointed lawyer, called the trial a “jurisprudential joke”.

In November 2025, a court in Dhaka sentenced her to death in absentia after finding her guilty on three counts of crimes against humanity, including incitement, ordering killings and failing to prevent atrocities.

Bangladesh’s foreign ministry has sought her extradition from India, which says the request is under legal review.

Her continued presence there has strained relations between the neighbouring countries.

She also faces a string of other cases, including corruption charges.

Hasina’s lawyers this week requested to renew her passport, without saying where or when she wished to travel.

Islam said the passport authority “may refuse to issue a passport” to anyone found guilty of serious crimes.

“Our advice to Sheikh Hasina would be, if you genuinely wish to return to Bangladesh, you should write to the Indian authorities and seek to facilitate your return under the extradition treaty,” he said.

Hasina’s pledge to return presents a political challenge for Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s government.

Many Bangladeshis want to see her hanged, while others fear her return could galvanise her former supporters and trigger a fresh confrontation between rival camps.

Police on Monday said they had arrested 12 people for a series of petrol bomb attacks, including against property, an empty bus and police vehicles this month. None of the attacks resulted in casualties.

Dhaka police spokesman Md Akhtar Hossain said the suspects were members of Hasina’s banned Awami League party.

Public university admission applications in January, exams to begin in February: UGC Chairman
item.description:
Applications for first-year undergraduate (honours) admission at the country’s public universities will begin in January next year, while admission tests are planned for February.

The decision was made at a meeting with vice-chancellors of public universities at the University Grants Commission (UGC) on Monday to discuss the schedule and other related matters for the 2026–27 academic year.

The meeting discussed students’ interests, admission test schedules, publication of results of the Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) supplementary examinations and coordination of the admission process.

It was also decided that universities will set and announce their examination dates through mutual coordination.

UGC Chairman Professor Mamun Ahmed shared the decisions at a press conference after the meeting.

The UGC chairman said the number of students who passed this year’s HSC and equivalent examinations was lower than last year. More than 700,000 students passed in 2025, while the figure was slightly over 600,000 in 2026.

He said answer scripts had been evaluated properly this year, as a result of which many students did not achieve their expected results. The authorities are arranging re-evaluation of answer scripts and supplementary examinations for these students.

The government is working towards publishing the results of the re-evaluation and supplementary examinations by 31 December. The public university admission process will begin after that, he said.

Students who pass the HSC supplementary examinations or obtain revised results following re-evaluation will be eligible to sit for university admission tests.

Mamun Ahmed said vice-chancellors had been asked to take the holy month of Ramadan into consideration when setting admission test schedules.

He also urged universities that have already announced their admission test dates to reconsider their schedules in the national interest and for the convenience of students.

item.title: NCP wants to keep Jamaat ‘in line’ while remaining in alliance
item.description:
The National Citizen Party (NCP), a partner in the same alliance, is dissatisfied with some of Jamaat-e-Islami’s recent political positions. The party’s policymakers believe Jamaat has become too accommodating towards the government in its role as an opposition party.

Against this backdrop, NCP has adopted a strategy of putting pressure on Jamaat still remaining part of the 11-party alliance. At the same time, the party wants to assert its own distinct political identity as well.

Prothom Alo learned of this stance after speaking to seven members of NCP’s political council, its highest policymaking body.

The growing distance between the two parties has come into focus through senior NCP leaders’ public criticism of Jamaat’s role in the recent by-election in Thakurgaon-1 and NCP’s limited participation in the 11-party alliance’s Khulna divisional long march on 31 October. NCP leaders, however, have said they do not want to leave the alliance.

NCP has adopted a strategy of putting pressure on Jamaat still remaining part of the 11-party alliance. At the same time, the party wants to assert its own distinct political identity as well.

In September, almost all the senior leaders of NCP, including convener Nahid Islam and member secretary Akhtar Hossain, took part in person in the first two long marches organised by the Jamaat-led 11-party alliance.

However, NCP’s participation in the alliance’s Khulna divisional long march on 31 October was merely ‘symbolic’. The party’s two top leaders did not attend.

Instead, on the day before the Khulna long march, the NCP organised a mass protest programme in the capital’s Shahbagh area. The party also conducted a week-long publicity campaign around the programme. During that campaign, NCP leaders made no mention of the long march, although they had been quite vocal ahead of the previous two marches.

These developments surrounding the 31 October long march have brought renewed attention to the ‘distance’ between the NCP and its alliance partner, Jamaat.

NCP policymakers say recent developments have led them to believe that Jamaat is forgetting its role as a genuine opposition party and becoming too accommodating towards the government. The NCP wants to put pressure on Jamaat to prevent it from becoming overly ‘effusive’ towards the government or the ruling party.

A senior NCP leader said they wanted to keep Jamaat ‘in line’ by criticising it while remaining in the 11-party alliance. This would also help counter what the leader described as ‘malicious propaganda’ claiming that the NCP was being absorbed into Jamaat. It would therefore help the party preserve its distinct identity.

NCP policymakers say recent developments have led them to believe that Jamaat is forgetting its role as a genuine opposition party and becoming too accommodating towards the government. NCP wants to put pressure on Jamaat to prevent it from becoming overly ‘effusive’ towards the government or the ruling party.

Public criticism over the Thakurgaon by-election

Voting in the by-election for the Thakurgaon-1 constituency took place on 29 October. Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) candidate Mirza Faisal Amin (brother of President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir) was unofficially declared elected after securing 227,917 votes.

His closest rival, Jamaat candidate Delawar Hossain, received 96,513 votes. The gap between the winning and losing candidates was 131,404 votes.

However, even before the results were announced, Jamaat called a protest, alleging irregularities, ballot stuffing and that polling agents had been beaten and forced out of polling stations.

Mirza Faisal visits defeated Jamaat candidate’s home with bouquet; Delwar says, ‘Best of luck’

But the following day, around noon, the winning BNP candidate visited the Jamaat candidate’s home with a bouquet of flowers. The two embraced and exchanged sweets. They also expressed their resolve to work together for the development of the area.

While this was happening in Thakurgaon, the picture in Dhaka was quite different. On the afternoon of 30 October, Jamaat Secretary General Mia Golam Porwar held a press conference at the party’s central office in Moghbazar in the capital.

He said ballot papers had been stamped in advance, fake votes cast and polling agents driven out of polling stations during the Thakurgaon-1 by-election.

If the Election Commission secretary and chief denied the irregularities, it would mean that the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and the EC secretary had colluded with those responsible. They had failed to do justice to their constitutional positions, he added.

NCP leaders publicly criticised what they described as Jamaat’s ‘double standards’. The first to speak out was former adviser to the interim government and NCP Senior Joint Member Secretary Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain. Hasnat Abdullah, a member of parliament and NCP senior joint convener, also criticised the party.

Hasnat Abdullah We cannot claim from Dhaka that there was vote rigging and then accept the results. That is not how an opposition party should act. We cannot say there was vote rigging and then go and exchange sweets. That is not what opposition means.

Speaking at a mass protest in Shahbagh on the afternoon of 30 October, Asif Mahmud said, “There was a by-election in Thakurgaon. From the morning, we saw presiding officers in various places stamping ballot papers in advance, and they were caught doing so.”

“What is deeply disappointing is that we see the candidate from the ruling party and the opposition candidate exchanging sweets with each other. Our democracy is going through a period of severe crisis and distress,” he added.

Hasnat Abdullah also criticised Jamaat’s role in the Thakurgaon by-election while attending a roadside rally in Jashore as an NCP representative during the Khulna long march.

Although he did not name any party, Hasnat said, “We cannot claim from Dhaka that there was vote rigging and then accept the results. That is not how an opposition party should act. We cannot say there was vote rigging and then go and exchange sweets. That is not what opposition means.”

Tensions between NCP leadership and Samanta stretched back months

Following these public remarks by Asif Mahmud and Hasnat Abdullah, discussion about the ‘distance’ between Jamaat and NCP has intensified in political circles. Over the past few days, supporters of the two parties have also made posts countering eac other on Facebook.

Various Facebook accounts supporting Jamaat have claimed that the NCP wants Jamaat’s backing in at least one of the two Dhaka city corporation elections in the upcoming local government polls. According to these accounts, the NCP is trying to put pressure on Jamaat in order to secure that support.

However, NCP Joint Convener Ariful Islam Adeeb told Prothom Alo, “Some of Jamaat’s political positions are creating distrust among the public. For example, it makes very strong statements on the streets but takes the opposite position in parliament, and gives the government its blank support during labour movements.”

“That is why we have taken a separate position. Our stance is essentially political. There is no question of bargaining here,” he added.

NCP Joint Convener Sarwar TusherBreaking up the alliance or creating a rift within it, is part of the government’s agenda. We are not falling into that trap.

Behind the ‘rift’

Prothom Alo spoke to seven members of NCP’s political council, the party’s highest policymaking body, to understand the reasons behind the apparent ‘rift’ between the NCP and Jamaat.

They said NCP has come to feel that Jamaat did not want to put pressure on the government during its first two years in office. Instead, it wanted to proceed somewhat cautiously and take things slowly.

The NCP, however, does not agree with this approach. It is therefore maintaining its own distinct tone, which is at times creating distance between the two parties, they said.

One member of NCP’s political council said, “When Jamaat tries to put pressure on the government over various issues and then holds formal or informal discussions with it, the party becomes somewhat accommodating. This has an impact on the other parties in the opposition alliance.”

“When Jamaat puts pressure on the government, the other parties also adopt the same stance. But when it suddenly becomes accommodating, the other parties are left in an awkward position. This is what we are trying to address,” added the NCP leader.

An NCP policymaker said that whenever the 11-party alliance takes a political position, it should be based on discussions involving all the parties in the alliance.

Speaking to Prothom Alo, he said that when Jamaat suddenly adopts a more accommodating stance towards the BNP without informing the other parties, it creates an awkward situation. If being accommodating towards the government is part of a strategy, the other alliance partners should also be informed.

Leaders of the party said NCP has come to feel that Jamaat did not want to put pressure on the government during its first two years in office. Instead, it wanted to proceed somewhat cautiously and take things slowly.

The leader also cited several reasons behind this perception of NCP. These included Jamaat Ameer and opposition leader Shafiqur Rahman’s demand for a special committee on constitutional reform during the first session of the current parliament on 31 March. He had proposed that the committee have equal numbers of members from the ruling and opposition parties.

NCP was also uncomfortable with Shafiqur Rahman’s remarks in parliament on 7 September that the ongoing energy crisis was not caused by the current government. The party also believes that Jamaat’s initial position on the recent labour protests was not appropriate.

NCP leaders said they wanted to keep pressure on Jamaat to ensure that it properly fulfils its role as an opposition party. They said NCP wanted to pursue genuine opposition politics. They also claimed that Jamaat had changed its earlier positions on several issues as a result of pressure from the NCP.

Despite seeking to put pressure on Jamaat, NCP has no intention of leaving the 11-party alliance. On this, the party’s Joint Convener Sarwar Tusher told Prothom Alo, “Breaking up the alliance or creating a rift within it, is part of the government’s agenda. We are not falling into that trap.”

item.title: Nine industrial groups join the billion-dollar club
item.description:
The 2025–26 financial year was not particularly favourable for the country's industrial sector. Energy shortages disrupted factory production, while exports recorded no significant growth.

Despite these challenges, nine industrial groups in Bangladesh crossed the one billion dollar threshold in import and export trade, including customs duties and taxes. In the 2024–25 financial year, eight industrial groups featured on this list.

The nine industrial groups that joined the billion-dollar club in import and export trade by the end of the last financial year are Meghna Group of Industries (MGI), PRAN-RFL Group, South Korea's Youngone Corporation, Abul Khair Group, Square Group, BSRM, TK Group, Khair Kashem Group and Ha-Meem Group.

City Group was also a member of this club a year ago. However, the import and export trade of this leading industrial group, which is currently facing difficulties, declined by 41 per cent in a year.

As a result, its trade volume fell below the billion-dollar club's threshold of one billion dollar.

Meanwhile, Khair Kashem Group entered the club for the first time after acquiring several operational factories. Ha-Meem Group also joined the list of successful exporters.

The remaining seven groups maintained billion-dollar transactions in their foreign trade during the last financial year, as they had done in the previous year.

According to data from the National Board of Revenue (NBR), the nine groups in the billion-dollar club imported goods worth US$9.83 billion during the last financial year.

In contrast, they exported goods worth approximately US$3.05 billion. They also paid Tk 199.44 billion, or around US$1.63 billion, in customs duties and taxes at the import stage.

Overall, the combined import and export trade of these nine groups amounted to US$14.55 billion. Excluding customs duties and taxes and considering only the value of imported and exported goods, the figure stood at US$12.87 billion, accounting for nearly 11 per cent of the country's total import and export trade during the last financial year.

The country's total import and export trade amounted to US$119.33 billion during the last financial year. Around 600,000 people work for the nine industrial groups in the billion-dollar club.

The term “billion-dollar club” refers to industrial groups whose annual trade reaches at least US$1 billion when import expenditure, including customs duties and taxes, is combined with the value of exported goods and services (revenue from transporting goods on seagoing vessels). This does not represent the groups' total sales or profits.

Industrial groups generally do not disclose their annual transaction figures unless they are listed on the stock market. However, it is possible to identify the leading players among manufacturing companies engaged in import and export trade.

Three business models

The nine industrial groups in the billion-dollar club operate under three different business models.

Youngone Corporation and Ha-Meem Group are entirely export-oriented, with their export earnings exceeding their import expenditure.

PRAN-RFL Group and Square Group have established strong positions in both the domestic and export markets.

Meanwhile, MGI, Abul Khair Group, BSRM, TK Group and Khair Kashem Group primarily manufacture products for the domestic market. 

MGI leads the billion-dollar club

Meghna Group of Industries (MGI) has retained its top position in the billion-dollar club this year.

Including customs duties and taxes, the group's import and export trade amounted to approximately US$3.2691 billion in the last financial year, marking a 14 per cent increase compared with the previous financial year.

Mostafa Kamal, MGI Chairman We have not stopped investing in manufacturing industries despite the challenges. Our continuous investment has brought MGI to the top.

The group imported goods worth US$2.6717 billion and paid Tk 55.02 billion, or around US$450 million, in customs duties and taxes at the import stage. It also exported goods worth US$147.5 million.

MGI operates manufacturing facilities across at least 23 sectors. The group has a significant presence in sugar, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), edible oil, plastic raw materials, animal feed and seagoing vessels. Its fleet comprises 30 seagoing vessels.

Most of the group's factories manufacture products that serve as alternatives to imports. Entrepreneur Mostafa Kamal founded MGI 51 years ago. Its leading brand is “Fresh”. According to the group's information, around 68,000 people work for the company.

MGI Chairman Mostafa Kamal told Prothom Alo, "We have not stopped investing in manufacturing industries despite the challenges. Our continuous investment has brought MGI to the top. By manufacturing import-substitute products locally, we are saving foreign currency. We are now increasing investment in heavy and basic industries. Once the Cumilla Economic Zone becomes operational next year, six factories there will begin production. At the same time, we are expanding our fleet of seagoing vessels to increase export earnings. We want to maintain our passion for establishing new industries and creating employment opportunities."

PRAN-RFL: 19 per cent growth

PRAN-RFL Group ranks second on the list. Including customs duties and taxes, its import and export trade amounted to US$2.2622 billion, representing a 19 per cent increase compared with the previous financial year.

The group imported goods worth US$1.3965 billion and exported goods worth US$517.6 million. It paid Tk 42.57 billion in customs duties and taxes at the import stage.

The group's greatest strength lies in its extensive market reach. PRAN-RFL exported products to 129 countries during the last financial year. Non-garment products accounted for 77 per cent of its exports.

Ahsan Khan Chowdhury, PRAN-RFL Group Chairman and Chief Executive I believe PRAN-RFL will perform even better in the coming days. Bangladesh is one of the best countries in the world in terms of manufacturing, as production costs here are relatively low.

Its three largest markets were Saudi Arabia, the United States and India. The group is also one of the leading importers of capital machinery. It employs 204,000 people.

PRAN-RFL Group Chairman and Chief Executive Ahsan Khan Chowdhury told Prothom Alo, "We faced many challenges during the last financial year. Restrictions on exports to India through land ports and the war in the Middle East have reduced our competitiveness. We also struggled with energy shortages at home. Nevertheless, I believe PRAN-RFL will perform even better in the coming days. Bangladesh is one of the best countries in the world in terms of manufacturing, as production costs here are relatively low."

Youngone: Leading exporter

South Korea's Youngone Corporation is the only foreign company among the nine leading industrial groups.

The group's import and export trade amounted to US$1.7547 billion during the last financial year, marking a 15 per cent increase compared with the previous year. Although Youngone ranked third in terms of total trade, it topped the list of exporters.

During the last financial year, the group exported goods worth US$1.1161 billion. Its imports, including customs duties and taxes, amounted to US$638.5 million. In other words, Youngone's export earnings were almost 1.75 times its import expenditure.

Garments accounted for 94 per cent of Youngone's exports, with high-value jackets and outdoor clothing making up a significant proportion. The group exported products to 62 countries during the last financial year. Its major markets include the United States, Germany and China.

Youngone began its operations in Bangladesh around 45 years ago. The group established the country's first privately owned Export Processing Zone (EPZ), the Korean EPZ, in Anwara, Chattogram.

According to the group's information, more than 80,000 people work at its factories in Chattogram and Dhaka.

Kihak Sung, Youngone Corporation Chairman A sufficient and reliable energy supply is essential for Youngone to implement its investment plans and expand high-value garment manufacturing in Bangladesh.

Youngone Corporation Chairman Kihak Sung told Prothom Alo that the company wanted to increase the production of synthetic fibre-based products at the Korean EPZ and bring more stages of the manufacturing process under its direct management.

However, inadequate energy supply remains a major obstacle to expansion. This has limited opportunities to increase the production of synthetic fibre-based products and make new investments.

A sufficient and reliable energy supply is essential for Youngone to implement its investment plans and expand high-value garment manufacturing in Bangladesh.

Abul Khair Group: Focus on raw materials for heavy industries

Abul Khair Group, which ranks fourth in the billion-dollar club, imported goods worth approximately US$1.236 billion during the last financial year.

It paid Tk 39.33 billion (around US$321.5 million) in revenue at the import stage. Overall, the group's import and export trade amounted to US$1.6 billion during the last financial year.

Around 95 per cent of the group's imports consist of industrial raw materials. It has a strong presence in several sectors, including steel rods, cement, corrugated iron sheets, powdered milk, tea and tobacco.

During the last financial year, the group exported goods worth approximately US$43 million. Tobacco accounted for 83 per cent of its exports, with the United States serving as a major destination.

The group is also increasing investment in new sectors. Alongside expanding its steel production capacity, it has invested in the pharmaceutical and jute industries. The group began exporting pharmaceutical products during the last financial year.

Founded in 1953, the group has grown into one of the country's leading industrial conglomerates under the leadership of Abul Khair's sons.

It currently operates nearly 50 companies across various sectors, including steel, cement, shipping and ceramics. The group employs around 60,000 people.

Square Group: Pharmaceuticals at home, garments abroad

Among the industrial groups on the list, Square Group exports products to the second-highest number of countries after PRAN-RFL Group, reaching 97 countries.

Including customs duties and taxes, the group's import and export trade amounted to US$1.2177 billion, representing a 1 per cent increase compared with the 2024–25 financial year.

During the last financial year, the group imported goods worth approximately US$710 million and exported goods worth around US$410 million. It paid the Government Tk 12.84 billion, or approximately US$105 million, in revenue at the import stage.

Square's pharmaceutical business primarily depends on the domestic market. In contrast, ready-made garments account for 89 per cent of its export earnings. The remaining earnings come from pharmaceuticals, food products and cosmetics.

MD Tapan Chowdhury, Managing Director, Square Textiles Chairman and Square Pharmaceuticals We are placing greater emphasis on making our business sustainable by reducing production waste and adopting environmentally friendly manufacturing practices.

Asked about the matter, Square Textiles Chairman and Square Pharmaceuticals Managing Director (MD) Tapan Chowdhury told Prothom Alo, "We are not setting up any new factories at present. Alongside improving product quality, we have started exporting high-value textile products, particularly denim fabrics and high-value ready-made garments. In addition, we are placing greater emphasis on making our business sustainable by reducing production waste and adopting environmentally friendly manufacturing practices."

BSRM: A billion dollars in a single sector

BSRM ranks sixth in the billion-dollar trade list, having achieved this milestone solely through its steel business.

During the last financial year, the group imported goods worth US$1.0635 billion. It paid Tk 9.97 billion (US$80 million) in customs duties and taxes at the import stage.

It also exported goods worth approximately US$20 million. Including customs duties and taxes, its total import and export trade amounted to US$1.1667 billion.

Around 98 per cent of its imports consist of steel raw materials sourced from 70 countries. The group sells almost all the steel manufactured from these materials in the domestic market.

Aameir Alihussain, Managing Director, BSRM We plan to increase investment in this sector to sustain our growth.

Its export products include zinc ash, zinc oxide and slag, which are by-products of its manufacturing operations. The group's two stock market-listed companies recorded combined business worth approximately Tk 240 billion during the last financial year.

Founded in 1952, the group is now under the leadership of its third generation. Despite declining demand for steel, BSRM says it has maintained growth and is planning further investments.

BSRM Managing Director Aameir Alihussain told Prothom Alo, "Although overall demand for steel has declined, we have maintained our growth. This is because our products are of good quality. We plan to increase investment in this sector to sustain our growth. If we receive policy support, we want to establish a steel plate manufacturing factory in Mirsharai at a cost of Tk 100 billion."

TK Group: Edible oil drives major business

TK Group imported goods worth US$960 million during the last financial year. It paid Tk 19.05 billion (approximately US$155 million) in customs duties and taxes. The group's exports amounted to US$10 million.

Overall, its import and export trade totalled approximately US$1.1258 billion, marking a 2 per cent decline compared with the previous financial year.

Around 98 per cent of TK Group's imports consist of primary and intermediate industrial raw materials. A significant proportion of these materials comprises crude palm oil and soybean oil.

Other imports include raw materials for corrugated iron sheets, LPG and chemicals. Most of the group's export earnings come from crust leather. It also exports food products, steel and chemicals. The group employs around 35,000 people.

Muhammad Mustofa Haider, Director, TK Group There are many global challenges at present. Nevertheless, we are expanding our business gradually, step by step, in line with our plans.

Samuda Group, an associate of TK Group, is currently expanding its business. It is increasing its operations in petrochemicals, synthetic yarn and soybean crushing.

Asked about the matter, TK Group Director Muhammad Mustofa Haider told Prothom Alo, "There are many global challenges at present. Nevertheless, we are expanding our business gradually, step by step, in line with our plans."

Khair Kashem Group: A new entrant on the list

Khair Kashem Group has joined the billion-dollar club for the first time. Abul Kashem, Chairman of Abul Khair Group, has established this separate industrial group outside his existing business conglomerate.

The group's principal company is Smile Food Products Limited. In March and December 2024, the group acquired five companies, including a seed-crushing factory, a sugar refinery and three ready-made garment factories.

The group now comprises nine companies in total. Following the acquisitions, the factories concerned began full-scale production during the last financial year. This development enabled the group to enter the billion-dollar club for the first time.

During the last financial year, the group imported goods worth US$861.6 million, paid US$173.2 million in customs duties and taxes, and exported goods worth US$39.3 million. Its total import and export trade amounted to US$1.0741 billion. Around 98 per cent of its imports relate to the edible oil and sugar sectors.

Ha-Meem Group: Exports 2.5 times its imports

Ha-Meem Group has also entered the billion-dollar list for the first time this year.

The group exported goods worth US$751.6 million during the last financial year, while its imports amounted to US$298 million. In other words, its exports were two-and-a-half times the value of its imports, the highest ratio among the nine groups.

As the group imports raw materials under the bonded warehouse facility, its customs duties and taxes at the import stage amounted to only Tk 210 million.

Even excluding customs duties and taxes, Ha-Meem's combined import and export trade exceeded US$1 billion. Overall, its import and export trade amounted to US$1.05 billion.

Ha-Meem is the leading exporter among domestic industrial groups. Besides garments, the group operates businesses in tea estates, printing, media and jute mills.

AK Azad, Ha-Meem Group Managing Director The group had increased its production capacity in various ways, placing particular emphasis on adopting automated technologies in manufacturing over the past few years. This had boosted production, delivering positive results for the business

Asked about the matter, Ha-Meem Group Managing Director AK Azad told Prothom Alo that working with renowned international brands had helped the group expand its business. He added that the group had also increased its production capacity in various ways, placing particular emphasis on adopting automated technologies in manufacturing over the past few years. This had boosted production, delivering positive results for the business.

AK Azad expressed hope that the group would maintain its growth in the future, provided the country's overall law and order situation remained stable, labour unrest did not occur and no new uncertainties emerged.

Asked about the matter, Centre for Policy Dialogue (CPD) Distinguished Fellow Mustafizur Rahman told Prothom Alo that these groups, which started as small and medium-sized enterprises, had now achieved transaction volumes exceeding US$1 billion.

He said, "The hard work and expertise of entrepreneurs, together with government policy support, have helped them reach this stage. Policy support is also necessary to ensure that current small and medium-sized entrepreneurs have opportunities to achieve similar success. Although large industrial groups can overcome various challenges, small and medium-sized entrepreneurs do not have the same capacity. In an economy like Bangladesh's, the number of such successful businesses should be much higher. We also need to analyse the circumstances of those whose trade volumes have fallen below the one billion dollar threshold."

item.title: PM leaves tomorrow for COP31 summit in Turkiye
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman will leave here tomorrow for Türkiye to attend the COP31 World Leaders' Summit, where he will address a plenary session and hold bilateral meetings on the sidelines.

The summit is scheduled to take place in Antalya on 11-12 November, with the Prime Minister set to deliver Bangladesh's statement at a plenary session on 12 November.

COP, officially known as the Conference of the Parties, is the annual United Nations climate summit where countries discuss collective action to address climate change.

Newly appointed Foreign Secretary Salahuddin Noman Chowdhury briefed reporters on preparations for the visit at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs today.

The Prime Minister will undertake the official visit from 10 to 12 November to lead the Bangladesh delegation.

His spouse Zubaida Rahman, the Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, the two state ministers for foreign affairs, the Prime Minister's Special Assistant on Environment, Forest and Climate Change, relevant government officials, a media team and other distinguished individuals will accompany him.

The foreign secretary said arrangements for the Prime Minister's engagements on the sidelines of the summit were still being finalised.

Bilateral meetings are being arranged with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, the Australian Prime Minister, the President of Uzbekistan and the British Foreign Secretary.

PM Tarique Rahman’s three-country tour planned for October, November

A meeting with the Administrator of the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is also being explored.

The meetings are expected to cover strengthening bilateral relations, expanding trade and investment, cooperation in addressing climate change and other matters of mutual interest.

Chowdhury expressed the hope that these engagements would create new opportunities to advance Bangladesh's economic and geopolitical interests.

Responding to a question about a possible courtesy meeting between the Prime Minister and the Turkish President, he said there was a possibility of such an engagement, during which overall cooperation between the two countries would be discussed.

The two sides could discuss the broader relationship, but specific project arrangements were unlikely to be settled during a courtesy meeting on the sidelines of a multilateral conference, he said.

Asked about Turkish company Çelebi’s interest in providing ground handling services at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport's third terminal as a partner of Biman Bangladesh Airlines under the Japanese consortium, he said detailed discussions on that particular proposal were unlikely during such a meeting.

On compensation for climate-related losses and damage, Chowdhury said Bangladesh presents estimates of the damage it has suffered before international forums to raise awareness and mobilise cooperation.

He said there were various estimates of Bangladesh's climate-related losses, which the country highlights in global discussions.

90 million displaced people at climate risk in Bangladesh, other countries: UNHCR

Presenting these concerns internationally helps create awareness about Bangladesh's situation and works in the country's favour, he added.

Asked how much compensation Bangladesh had secured through the COP process, the foreign secretary said the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change would be able to provide the relevant information.

He also distinguished compensation from the broader assistance and cooperation Bangladesh receives through presenting its position in international forums.

In his plenary address, the Prime Minister will outline Bangladesh's position and expectations on climate justice, the historical responsibility of developed countries, climate finance, adaptation, addressing loss and damage, and climate-resilient sustainable development.

Chowdhury said Bangladesh contributes only 0.05 per cent of global greenhouse gas emissions, yet remains among the countries most vulnerable to the adverse impacts of climate change.

Against this backdrop, securing climate justice is one of Bangladesh's foremost priorities, he said.

Other priorities include adaptation finance, addressing loss and damage, and ensuring the effective implementation of developed countries' climate finance commitments.

At the summit, Bangladesh will highlight its achievements in climate resilience and share its experience in addressing climate impacts across South Asia and the wider Asian region.

Bangladesh has also taken an initiative to establish a jute pavilion in the conference's Green Zone to showcase jute's diverse uses, environmentally friendly characteristics and potential as an alternative to plastic.

PM urges global leaders to turn climate pledges into action

A joint declaration between Bangladesh and Turkiye on the use and promotion of jute and jute products is also envisaged during the conference, the foreign secretary said.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs will organise two side events in the Blue Zone on 12 and 13 November.

One will focus on gender-based vulnerability in Bangladesh resulting from the adverse impacts of climate change, while the other will address the challenges of promoting environmentally friendly, biodegradable and zero-waste jute products.

The events will draw international attention to the particular risks women face because of climate change and the scope for expanding the use of jute products as alternatives to synthetic polymer-based products.

Chowdhury said Trkiye is presiding over this year's conference, while Australia is co-chairing the formal climate negotiation process.

He said the Ministry of Foreign Affairs had coordinated with the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change and other relevant ministries and agencies to prepare for Bangladesh's participation.

The country's positions and priorities were determined through inter-ministerial discussions and consultations with stakeholders, he added.

The foreign secretary expressed the hope that Bangladesh's participation under the Prime Minister's leadership would strengthen its position in international climate diplomacy and provide an opportunity to showcase its efforts and achievements in building climate resilience.

Additional Foreign Secretary (Public Diplomacy and Other Priority Matters) AKM Shahidul Karim and senior ministry officials were present at the briefing.

item.title: Government stocks of rice, wheat rise, but distribution declines
item.description:
Arambagh slum in Rupnagar, Mirpur, is quite large, home to thousands of low-income people. In the past, the government used to sell food items at subsidised prices from trucks parked in front of the slum. Residents could not recall which agency operated the sales, but they said they used to queue up to buy the food. That service is no longer available.

Sufia Begum, 45, lives in the slum. She was found in front of Arambagh slum on Sunday. She told Prothom Alo that she previously had a Trading Corporation of Bangladesh (TCB) card, which allowed her to buy rice, lentils, oil, sugar and other essentials at subsidised prices. Her card has since been cancelled. Trucks selling government-subsidised rice and flour no longer come to the slum.

Sufia said her husband used to sell dried fish and vegetables from a roadside stall, but he can no longer set up his shop. She herself worked at a garment factory but lost her job after breaking her arm. Her family is now struggling financially.

Many people like Sufia and her family are facing hardship. Meanwhile, the government has substantial stocks of rice and wheat. However, at a time when people are struggling, the distribution of government rice and wheat has declined.

Economists say inflation remains high in the country, while various studies indicate that poverty has increased. At such a time, the government should release more food into the market so that people facing renewed financial difficulties in both urban and rural areas can buy essentials at lower prices.

According to the Ministry of Food, the government currently has slightly more than 2.1 million tonnes of rice and wheat in stock, including around 1.8 million tonnes of rice and 300,000 tonnes of wheat. In June 2024, towards the end of the Awami League government's tenure, which was ousted following the July mass uprising, food stocks stood at 1.47 million tonnes.

During the tenure of the interim government, food stocks exceeded 2 million tonnes. On 4 January, Ali Imam Majumder, food adviser to the former interim government, told journalists that food stocks were at their highest level in five years. He described the stock situation as highly satisfactory.

The current stock is more than 600,000 tonnes higher than what the Awami League government had at the end of its tenure. It has also increased further compared with the interim government's period.

According to the latest data from the Ministry of Food, the government distributed 1.104 million tonnes of food grains between July and October, the first four months of the 2026–27 fiscal year. This was 67,000 tonnes less than in the same period of the previous fiscal year.

The government maintains food grain stocks in its warehouses to support poor people and stabilise the market. Rice and wheat are the main commodities stored. A portion of these stocks is sold at subsidised prices, while another portion is distributed as relief and assistance.

The government's largest programme is the Food-Friendly Programme. Under this initiative, 5.5 million people receive rice at Tk 15 per kg for six months a year- from March to April, and from August to November. Each beneficiary receives 30kg of rice per month.

The Open Market Sale (OMS) programme runs throughout the year. Under this initiative, rice and flour are sold year-round through designated dealers' shops and mobile trucks.

Rice under the Food-Friendly Programme is distributed against beneficiary cards. Those without cards cannot access this assistance. For them, the only options are OMS shops or mobile sales trucks.

According to the Ministry of Food, around 268,000 tonnes of rice and wheat were allocated under the OMS programme between July and October, 93,000 tonnes or 26 per cent less than in the same period of the previous year.

A report by the World Food Programme (WFP), published on 22 September, said the number of people in Bangladesh at risk of acute food insecurity could reach 18.1 million between September and December this year, an increase of 2.8 million from the beginning of the year.

The report cited inflation, declining purchasing power, agricultural losses caused by floods, child malnutrition and uncertainty over food assistance for Rohingya refugees as contributing factors.

In other words, the number of people at risk of food insecurity has increased, but government allocations have declined.

Saving Tk 20 per kg

The lowest price of coarse rice in Dhaka markets is currently Tk 50 per kg. Slightly better-quality coarse rice sells for Tk 55 per kg. Rice prices have remained largely unchanged over the past month, but they have not declined significantly either.

The government sells rice under the OMS programme at Tk 30 per kg. This allows low-income consumers to save Tk 20 on every kilogram they buy.

The government sells flour at Tk 24 per kg, while loose flour in the market costs Tk 48–50 per kg. This means consumers can save Tk 24–26 per kg by purchasing flour through the OMS programme.

A 2025 survey by the private research organisation Power and Participation Research Centre (PPRC) found that nearly 55 per cent of a household's monthly expenditure in Bangladesh goes towards food purchases.

Poor families spend a significant portion of their income on rice and flour. Savings on these essentials could provide some relief.

Amena Begum, 60, lives in a slum near the Shaheed Buddhijibi Graveyard in Mirpur Section 1. She runs her household by selling bread. Speaking to Prothom Alo on Sunday, she said, "Prices of everything in the market are high. The government provides so many kinds of assistance, but nobody even puts our names on the list."

Many people depend on rice sold under the OMS programme. One of them is Afia Begum, a resident of the Ispahani Sea Gate Gol Pahar slum in Chattogram city.

She told Prothom Alo that she now receives 5kg of rice once a month through the OMS programme at Tk 30 per kg. However, the rice supplied is atop rice (non-parboiled), rather than coarse rice. Her family is not accustomed to eating atop variety, but they buy it because of the price. Purchasing rice from the open market would cost Tk 55–60 per kg.

Afia also said TCB currently provides two litres of oil, one kilogramme of sugar, one kilogramme of salt and a bar of soap. She does not really need the soap but needs rice and onions. TCB used to provide rice two years ago, but no longer does so.

Why has distribution declined?

Alongside the Directorate General of Food, the government occasionally distributes rice through the state-owned Trading Corporation of Bangladesh (TCB).

The Directorate General of Food claims that the overall allocation has declined because no rice was allocated for TCB during the current fiscal year.

Md Jamal Hossain, additional director general of the Directorate General of Food, told Prothom Alo that no allocation had been made for TCB during the first four months of the fiscal year. The Ministry of Finance allocated 300,000 tonnes of rice for TCB from November. The distribution declined mainly because there was no allocation during the first four months, he said.

Through its Smart Family Cards, TCB provides around 7.5 million families with essential commodities such as oil, lentils and sugar at subsidised prices every month.

During periods of crisis, it also sells goods from mobile trucks outside the regular card-based programme. Long queues of people are often seen waiting to buy these products. Many return empty-handed because supplies run out.

In addition to oil and sugar, TCB occasionally distributed rice as well.

TCB spokesperson Shahadat Hossain told Prothom Alo on Sunday that the corporation had been corresponding with the authorities for four months to secure a rice allocation but had not received any so far. He hoped the allocation would come this month.

Food distribution needs to be increased

Inflation has remained high in Bangladesh since 2022. The recent conflict in the Middle East has pushed up prices of various commodities in Bangladesh, including fuel and cooking gas. Meanwhile, wages are increasing at a slower rate than inflation.

The government has started providing cash assistance through Family Cards, but the programme has yet to expand significantly.

Selim Raihan, a professor of economics at Dhaka University and executive director of the South Asian Network on Economic Modeling (SANEM), told Prothom Alo that during periods of crisis, poor people often have no option but to cut their food expenditure. They skip a meal or get by on half a meal. Government assistance does not reach everyone. Therefore, subsidised food distribution needs to be increased.

He added that poverty has increased in the country, which is a warning sign. The government needs to introduce large-scale assistance programmes at such a time.

Selim Raihan further said the government had substantial food stocks, which was a positive development. However, distribution needed to be increased.

Government to procure paddy and rice

Meanwhile, the government has decided to procure 300,000 tonnes of paddy and 550,000 tonnes of rice during the current Aman season.

The procurement prices have been set at Tk 35 per kg for paddy, Tk 49 for parboiled rice and Tk 48 for non-parboiled rice.

Food Minister Afroza Khanam disclosed the information at a press conference held at the Press Information Department's conference room at the Secretariat on Sunday.

She said procurement of Aman paddy would begin on 24 November and continue until 28 February 2027. Rice procurement would begin on 1 December and also continue until 28 February.
